programmes.d: Tennis great Bjorn Borg rolls a clip from his 5th Wimbledon victory. Chats about going pro at 15 and how he keeps his cool on the court while other players throw tantrums.
Johnny's favorite baseball player Bob Uecker talks about his New TV series Mr. Belvedere, collecting baseball cards, and his various commercial endeavors.
Baseball star Joe Garagiola shows his first contract, with the St. Louis Cardinals, to prove the paltry players' pay back in the day compared to fat checks handed to today's pros.
Baseball legend Joe Garagiola demonstrates how players put more spin on the ball by scuffing it with a cork. Also shows a fascinating clip of great mistakes in baseball.
Tennis star Pete Sampras celebrates his first major title at the US Open. Knick named "pistol Pete" for his powerful serve, Sampras says his victory over Andre Agassi will not change him.
Animal trainer Joan Embery introduces Johnny to a wide variety of animals, including a baby gorilla, tiger, cougar and a 13-foot python. Also featured are David Brenner and the Amazing Kreskin.
Celebrate New Year's day with Foster Brooks, Victor Buono and.....Joan Embery and her gorilla friends.
Bubble the Hippo makes an appearance (!) with animal trainer Joan Embery. Competing with Bubbles for cutest animal on the show are twin baby orangutans and a horned frog.

Animal expert Jim Fowler brings out an alligator and crocodile and explains to Johnny the difference between the two. Not to be outdone, Rodney Dangerfield has Johnny in stitches with his non-stop one-liners.
If you've ever wondered what an aardvark looks like, this episode is for you. Also featured is comedian David Steinberg, who does a hilarious Ed Sullivan impression.
Animal trainer Jim Fowler brings a baby baboon and golden eagle onto the set, and Johnny's next guest, writer Gore Vidal, exclaims that he should have brought his pet lizard.
Saturday Night Live performer Mary Gross does an imitation of Marilyn Monroe, and Joan Embery brings out a hyena, penguin and baby gorilla.
Frequent guest Joan Rivers discusses her autobiography, and Joan Embery bring a rare Albino Koala Bear to the show.
Joan Embery of the San Diego Zoo visits Johnny with a pair of Orangutans, joining Danny Devito, who discusses his film "Ruthless People."
Who doesn't love a Koala bear? When Johnny holds the bear, the Koala doesn't want to let go so Joan Embery has to pry the bear away.
Jim Fowler, the host of "Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom," brings an Indian Condor onto the show. Also featured is comedian Bob Nelson.
On this diverse episode, the legendary Jimmy Stewart reads a poem, and animal trainer Jim Fowler brings a 220-pound Python on stage. Holy juxtaposition!
Jay Leno describes his parents amazingly happy marriage, his busy stand-up schedule and getting recognized in a New York City deli.
Astrophysicist and Pulitzer prize winner, Carl Sagan shares how he realized that he wanted to study astronomy. Also discusses how he thinks Americans would handle the arrival of extra-terrestrials.
Host of The Today Show Tom Brokaw chats about People naming him sexiest man alive. Also explains how he functions so early in the morning and details his tricks for interviewing politicians.
Celebrated news anchor Walter Cronkite thinks people should get their news from books and newspapers as well as television. Also explains interview diplomacy.
One of the world's most influential journalists, Barbara Walters describes dealing with touchy heads of state and getting Christmas cards from world leaders.
The world's leading authority on chimpanzees, Jane Goodall describes how these primates mirror humans in that they can make and use tools and that they have distinct personalities.
Olympic gold medalist Caitlyn Jenner says she's now into tennis and working hard on her talk/variety show America Alive. Next up: hosting the 1980 Olympics in Moscow.
"Mr. Baseball" Bob Uecker complains about his modest player's salary compared to today's whooping paydays. Also jokes that he's the only player paid NOT to do product endorsements.
Tennis great Bjorn Borg rolls a clip from his 5th Wimbledon victory. Chats about going pro at 15 and how he keeps his cool on the court while other players throw tantrums.
